source_refs.note: 'Supervised Machine Learning' under topic 6.4, as printed (PDF 80, printed 76).

blocks.text: Supervised machine learning uses labeled data for training. Each data item has an input and a correct output. The system learns by comparing its output with the correct answer. Supervised learning needs large labelled datasets, such as emails labelled as spam or not spam, images labelled as cat or dog, or medical scans labelled as normal or abnormal. Its accuracy usually improves when the model is trained on more high-quality examples. It is widely used in real applications, such as face recognition, disease detection, speech recognition, fraud detection, and recommendation systems. This method is used for prediction tasks. Examples include email spam detection and exam result prediction.
